method: Actual ordinary Windows app states reviewed through Computer Use. Desktop screenshot pixels were not saved or decoded. Native configuration and logs were independently read through the filesystem.

sessions.actualHelp: Default delay for the next media, in milliseconds at 100 ms steps. Current-media timing remains separate. Applies when the next media opens.
sessions.audioInterruption: Log records endpoints unplugged/not present, session disconnected: device removed, default output disabled and later active; stream invalidation and missing-default errors remain retained. Physical cause and complete recovery are unproven.

limits: The first ASS session is not a clean playback/audio regression pass; retain its device-removal failure separately from successful numeric-control/help observations.

Desktop observations establish displayed captions, controls, marker patterns and coarse elapsed time. Exact numeric conservation is not accepted: normalized position reconciles by about one microsecond during some changes.
Secondary-delay and subtitle-speed controls have names, but their backend timing semantics were not exercised here.
No audible-output, real device-loss recovery, screen-reader session, Windows DPI matrix or full-beta acceptance is claimed.
